name: Bodhi Monastery
tradition: Non-sectarian Buddhism (Theravada/Pali roots with early Mahayana), inspired by Master Yin-Shun
technique: Samatha & Vipassana sitting meditation, walking meditation, daily chanting liturgy
teacherAccess: Resident monastics lead daily liturgy and meditation; visiting Theravada and Chan teachers (e.g. Sayadaw U Kovida, Ven. Bhikkhu Kaiyin) lead guided multi-day retreats with method instruction and Q&A.
retreatOptions: Free day-long weekend meditation sessions plus periodic residential silent retreats of 3, 7, 10, and up to 14 days (Samatha-Vipassana, Four Foundations of Mindfulness, Four Immeasurables) held on-site in the monastery's dormitories.
about: Bodhi Monastery is a Buddhist monastery set on 188 acres of woodlands and fields in Sussex County, New Jersey, founded to carry forward the non-sectarian vision of the Chinese scholar-monk Master Yin-Shun. Its resident monastics hold daily chanting and meditation, and the monastery periodically hosts multi-day residential silent meditation retreats led by visiting Theravada and Chan teachers, including week-long and two-week Samatha-Vipassana retreats organized jointly with teachers connected to the Pa-Auk meditation lineage. Retreatants stay in on-site dormitory housing, follow a full daily schedule of sitting and walking meditation, observe noble silence, and take vegetarian meals provided by the monastery. The monastery is closely associated with the scholar-monk Bhikkhu Bodhi, translator of the Pali Canon, and also runs a well-known food pantry program for the local community. All programs, including the residential retreats, are offered on a donation basis.
schedule: Weekly Sunday group sitting; free one-day weekend retreats; multi-day residential retreats (typically 3-14 nights) offered a few times per year, mainly in spring, summer, and fall.
cost: Donation-based (dana); no set fee for residential retreats, though participants are asked to help cover costs voluntarily.

pricePerDay.notes: No suggested amount; retreatants give as they are able.

foodNotes: Free vegetarian meals are provided during retreats and day programs.
workNotes: Retreatants are responsible for assigned chores (出坡) and keeping the meditation hall clean during residential retreats.
